2: GEMARA: 'And their slaughter is valid' after the fact - This [should be read as] a question [rather than a statement] (i.e., "And [is the Mishna saying that] their slaughter is valid after the fact?"). And the opening clause ("Everyone may slaughter") is difficult, for it implies that whoever is included in "everyone" is included ab initio. But if the latter clause ("and their slaughter is valid") implies that it is extending [the same meaning of] "everyone," then it would be extending [the same] to [encompass] an after-the-fact [slaughter], but we do not extend [the authorization to perform an act] ab initio [to encompass what is only acceptable] after the fact. And thus we cannot say that our Mishnah withholds something ab initio and that [only] one [thing] is taught. For since it is taught "Everyone may slaughter," it would be obvious that [their slaughter is] valid! [This would render the latter clause redundant.]
